pages.text: For days, the river kept rising. Soil at the yard's edge was damp. The three children carried soil to build a barrier.
Raju wanted to keep water out. "Let's build here first!"
Mina pointed elsewhere. "That side is lower." Mina used that path to fetch water every day.
Turning away and scooping soil, Raju said, "That's not right." Raju built only in the chosen spot.
They carried soil again and again. Raju's side reached knee-high.
The river rose farther all night.
In the morning, water entered from Mina's side. Raju stepped onto the soggy ground. Their foot sank in.
Looking at the muddy yard, Mom asked, "Which way do you go to fetch water?"
Raju followed Mina. Water still pooled on Mina's usual path.
All three piled soil high there. The next day, no more water entered the yard. Raju looked at Mina and nodded.
